text:
Recent work distinguishes excessive recency dependence from insufficient temporal sensitivity. “Measuring Recency Bias” (2024) reports that overemphasizing recent interactions can hurt recommendation accuracy; CETRec (2025), developed for LLM recommenders, distinguishes absolute order (recency) from relative order (transitions) through counterfactual tuning. These findings motivate separate probes for dependence on the latest items and dependence on their ordering; neither sensitivity nor invariance alone establishes good behavior. [Recency bias](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722), [CETRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03047).

Shuffling needs careful interpretation. RecSys 2025 research separates user behavior patterns from item-availability effects using constrained shuffling that prevents interactions preceding an item’s first observed appearance. Consequently, performance changes after unrestricted shuffling cannot automatically be attributed to learned preference transitions. CoDeR (2025) and CoDeR+ (2026) also investigate counterfactual reasoning about changing interests, but their modeling assumptions do not establish observed purchase intent. [Shuffling study](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042), [CoDeR](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/33379), [CoDeR+](https://doi.org/10.1145/3778863).

Suggested diagnostic synthesis: compare removal of recent versus older interactions, repeated-interest evidence versus isolated interactions, and local versus full shuffles. Match random controls on perturbation count and, where feasible, position and item frequency; preserve the item multiset for order probes. Hold candidates fixed and report paired rank changes, top-10 overlap, and validation HR@10 changes by category, with uncertainty across users. Define repeated interests using observed repeats or explicit title/description similarity, acknowledging that semantic similarity is a proxy. These interventions measure model reliance and robustness; they do not identify current intent or causal effects on user behavior.
